hypothese.summary: Q2 2026 confirms the central mechanism identified at creation (capex explosion → deferred pick-up in D&A compressing the margin) but with a magnitude and a timing significantly different from the initial estimates: actual D&A in H1 2026 (12,4 Md$) is well below the trajectory modelled at creation (which projected ~36 Md$ for the full year), which improves the margin in the near term but probably implies a later and more abrupt catch-up. Beyond that, reported operating income (-8% in Q2) masks a healthy underlying operational reality (+9% excluding non-recurring items, per the CFO herself): the decline is entirely due to 2,4 Md$ of legal charges and 1,2 Md$ of severance charges (May 2026 redundancy plan), not to a deterioration in the advertising business.
hypothese.text:
== THESIS SUMMARY ==
The central bet stands: Meta is running the heaviest investment cycle in its history (FY26 capex 130-145bn) to fund AI, with deferred D&A that will mechanically compress operating margin for several years regardless of product success. This refresh's good news: the ad core remains exceptional (Q2 revenue +28%, fastest in the industry), and the GAAP EPS miss (-14.5% vs consensus) is integrally attributable to 2.4bn one-off legal charges, not the operating engine.

== THESIS READ ==
- D&A recalibrated on real data: S1 actual 12.4bn vs ~18bn modeled at setup -> FY26 ~27bn, then a LATER, STEEPER catch-up (40bn 2027, 55bn 2028, 62-65bn 2029-30). The compression is deferred, not avoided. Watch: D&A run-rate each quarter - the single most model-sensitive line.
- FY26 EBIT anchored directly on guidance (revenue estimate minus guided total expenses at midpoint) rather than an independent margin assumption. Watch: any further expense-guidance creep from legal/regulatory items.
- Net debt appears (capex exceeds FCF at peak): ~30bn 2026, peaking ~55bn 2027 before receding. Watch: bond issuance terms and buyback pace trade-off.

== SPECIAL FACTORS ==
Pure GAAP base (no management-adjusted net exists). FY25 published net carries ~10bn of one-off tax charges (ETR 28.7% vs 16-17% normative) - the bridge documents it as residual; projections use normative rates (16.5% 2026, 17% 2027, 17.5% from 2028). EU DMA / US legal exposure remains the recurring one-off source.

== PARAMETERS & WATCH-LIST ==
Revenue +27% 2026 decelerating to +12% by 2030; EBIT margin trough 2027 (30%) then rebuild as D&A growth decelerates; shares -0.5%/yr net of SBC. Bridge finNet: interest on new debt net of cash yield. Watch: Reality Labs losses trajectory; ad pricing vs AI-capacity monetization evidence; consensus gap (Omnium 28.27 vs street 32.5 for 2026 - one-offs plus D&A phasing).

== CATALYSTS ==
Q3 (Oct); first AI-monetization disclosures; capex guidance for 2027 (Jan); legal-charge resolution.

ancrages.moteur: MAJOR CORRECTION this refresh (E6-a/E6-b): actual D&A in H1 2026 (12,4 Md$, of which 6,36 Md$ in Q2 alone) is well below the creation model's trajectory (~18 Md$ expected over the same period on the 50% ratio of n-1 capex with a one-year lag). FY2026 extrapolation revised to ~27 Md$ (vs ~36 Md$ at creation), the lag in bringing datacenters into service being longer than initially assumed. A more pronounced and later catch-up projected over 2027-2028 (40 Md$ then 55 Md$) before deceleration in 2029-2030 (62 Md$ then 65 Md$).

FY2026 EBIT anchored directly on the official Q2 2026 guidance: estimated revenue (~256 Md$, built bottom-up from actual H1 + Q3 guidance + Q4 estimate) less total guided expenses (165-169 Md$, midpoint 167 Md$) = ~89 Md$ - a more robust methodology than at creation (which started from a standalone margin assumption). Consistent with management's explicit reaffirmation that FY2026 operating income will exceed FY2025 (83,28 Md$).

The CFO explicitly confirms that excluding legal charges (2,4 Md$) and the severance charges of the May 2026 redundancy plan (1,2 Md$), Q2 2026 operating income would have risen +9% year on year (instead of the -8% reported) - the reported decline is entirely attributable to identified and quantified non-recurring items, not to a deterioration in the core advertising business (advertising revenue still growing the fastest in the industry, according to Zuckerberg). A qualitative item confirming the robustness of the operational base underlying the capex/D&A.

CORRECTION after verification (this refresh's initial calculation mistakenly applied the ACTUAL H1 2026 tax rate, itself distorted by the one-off tax benefit of 8,03 Md$ in Q1 2026 already identified at creation - reported H1 2026 shows a NEGATIVE TAX PROVISION of -2 113 M$, i.e. an implied ETR of -5,2%, against ~16% in Q2 alone excluding that effect). A normative tax rate is now applied CONSISTENTLY across the whole of FY2026 (17%, aligned with Q2 alone and with the official 15-17% guidance), rather than mixing the distorted actual H1 rate with a normative H2 rate - this avoids artificially carrying the one-off Q1 effect through into the annual projection. Rate held at 17% for 2027 then 17,5% (2028-2030).

Cash/net debt position ENTIRELY RECALIBRATED on the basis of the actual balance sheet at 30/06/2026 (residual net cash of only 6,6 Md$, against 22,9 Md$ modelled at end-FY2025): 25 Md$ of long-term debt issued in Q2 2026 alone, buybacks suspended, the CFO explicitly confirming a structural shift towards more debt-oriented funding. Swing into net debt projected as early as end-FY2026 (given the H2 capex still to be committed to reach the 130-145 Md$ guidance), peak modelled in 2027, then a decline as capex slows and FCF recovers with the ramp-up of D&A (non-cash) relative to cash capex.

Buybacks suspended in Q2 2026 (zero, against 10,2 Md$ in Q2 2025) in a context of prioritising the funding of capex - share count trajectory revised down in terms of pace of decline vs creation (which assumed buybacks would continue), share count broadly stable in the near term with a slight resumption of decline assumed from 2028 once the peak of the investment cycle is passed.

dernierCall.guidanceProchainTrimestre: Q3 2026 total revenue guided to $61-64B, assuming ~1pt FX headwind to YoY growth at current rates - implies continued mid-to-high-20s growth after Q2's +28% reported / +27% cc; guidance given with the usual caveat on active legal/regulatory matters (US youth-safety trials scheduled this year, potential material loss).
dernierCall.guidanceAnnuelle: FY2026 total expenses raised to $165-169B (lower end lifted to absorb the $2.4B Q2 legal charge; prior $162-169B). FY2026 capex, including finance-lease principal payments, narrowed upward to $130-145B (prior $125-145B). Tax rate for remaining 2026 quarters raised to 15-17% (prior 13-16%). FY2026 operating income explicitly reconfirmed above FY2025 ($83.28B) despite the expense raises. NO 2027 capex guidance provided; infrastructure plans geared to maximizing 2026-27 compute capacity (demand-constrained per the CFO), with land/power foundations laid for 2028+ flexibility and server purchase decisions deferred.
pointsCles: Underlying P&L intact despite the headline miss: CFO confirmed Q2 operating income would have grown +9% YoY excluding the $2.4B legal charges and $1.2B severance (May 2026 headcount reduction, ~8,000 roles; headcount 75,000+, -3% QoQ); reported operating margin fell to 31% on these one-offs, while the ramp in D&A remains the real recurring structural cost to monitor into 2027-2028.

AI monetization of the core is now quantified: Advantage+ crossed a $75B annual revenue run-rate; the GEM ads-ranking model plus the new Meta Generative Recommender drove +8.3% ad clicks and +15.7% conversions on Facebook (and +1% app-event conversions on Instagram); Family of Apps 'Other' revenue crossed $1B in a quarter for the first time (+73% YoY, WhatsApp paid messaging and subscriptions) - nascent diversification beyond pure advertising.

Capex regime and funding shift: quarterly capex hit $31.1B leaving FCF at just $784M; no 2027 capex guidance (Susan Li: infrastructure planning 'highly dynamic') but plans are explicitly geared to maximizing 2026-27 capacity - Meta describes itself as demand-constrained, including for the core business - with the funding mix tilting toward debt and infrastructure JVs (BlackRock, 1 GW El Paso data center under Meta Compute) and 2028+ server decisions deferred for flexibility.

Product pipeline is promise-heavy but staged: Zuckerberg frames consumer personal agents as a 'massive, near-inevitable' market within 5 years while conceding nothing has shipped yet; distinct from Business Agents already live globally (>1M businesses/week on WhatsApp/Messenger, Instagram rollout underway) and the Muse Spark public API (OpenRouter, enterprise rollout coming); return to open-source model releases promised 'soon' alongside closed frontier models, and Meta reports numerous offers to buy its compute 'at a significant premium'.
